leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: Oakland University (internal promotion; joined OU in 1993)
leaders.nextRole: Chief of Staff (retired from higher education)
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Celebrate Community Church, Sioux Falls, South Dakota
leaders.notes: Served as interim president from 1995 to 1996 (his true first year in the office, used here to anchor the chain), then as OU's substantive president until his abrupt June 2013 retirement, which came the same day his wife was fired as women's basketball coach. Led major campus expansion, OU's first strategic plan, and a $110M+ fundraising campaign.

leaders.priorTitle: Associate Vice President for Outreach and Executive Director of OU-Macomb
leaders.nextRole: Vice President for Organizational Development and Strategic Planning
leaders.notes: An OU alumna and career university president (previously president of Lake Superior State University and Western Oregon University, and chancellor of UW-Superior) who was in an OU-Macomb outreach role when tapped as interim president. After the interim term she became OU's VP for Organizational Development and Strategic Planning in September 2014.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Association of Governing Boards of Universities and Colleges (AGB)
leaders.notes: OU's 6th president; the board announced in September 2016 it would not renew his contract, which ended August 14, 2017. He was a finalist for the SIU Carbondale chancellorship in spring 2017 but withdrew, and later became a consultant with AGB.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President and U.S. Medical Leader, Lilly Biomedicines
leaders.notes: OU's 7th and current president (took office July 2017), a pediatric endocrinologist who previously was EVP for Medical Affairs and Health System CEO at the University of Michigan before her Eli Lilly role. No active presidential search was found; her contract was extended in 2023 through June 2031.

university: Oklahoma State University Center for Health Sciences

leaders.priorTitle: President of OSU-Tulsa (held concurrently); Tulsa businessman and former Oklahoma Secretary of Commerce
leaders.notes: Served as president of OSU Center for Health Sciences concurrently with the OSU-Tulsa presidency until Kayse Shrum was elevated to the CHS presidency in 2013, after which he continued to lead OSU-Tulsa. Start year (2009) is moderate confidence; the pre-2009 CHS leadership chain could not be verified because okstate.edu blocked automated access.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost of OSU-CHS and Dean of the OSU College of Osteopathic Medicine
leaders.priorInstitution: Oklahoma State University Center for Health Sciences (internal, since 2011)
leaders.nextRole: President (19th) of Oklahoma State University (system/main campus)
leaders.notes: Named OSU-CHS president in 2013, becoming the youngest and first female (and first alumna) president and dean of a medical school in Oklahoma. Left in 2021 to become OSU's 19th president; she resigned that system presidency in February 2025 and later returned to OSU-CHS as tenured faculty.

leaders.priorTitle: Chief Operating Officer and Senior Vice President
leaders.priorInstitution: Oklahoma State University Center for Health Sciences (internal)
leaders.notes: Named president of OSU Center for Health Sciences on September 10, 2021, after Shrum moved to the OSU system presidency; he had been the institution's COO and senior vice president. He was reported as interim first in mid-2021 before the permanent appointment.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the School of Medicine
leaders.priorInstitution: University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio
leaders.nextRole: Vice Chancellor for the Northwest Arkansas Region
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences (UAMS)
leaders.notes: OHSU's 3rd president; endocrinologist who led OHSU for 18 years (1988 to September 2006), through its 1995 transition to an independent public corporation. Immediately before OHSU he was dean of the UT medical school in San Antonio (from 1986); afterward he built UAMS's northwest Arkansas regional campus.

leaders.dean: Joseph E. Robertson Jr., M.D., M.B.A.
leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the School of Medicine and Director of the Casey Eye Institute
leaders.notes: OHSU's 4th president, from September 2006; a retinal surgeon who rose internally at OHSU. He entered PERS retirement effective Oct. 31, 2017 but continued as unpaid president through the transition (about June 2018) until Jacobs began August 1, 2018. He had multiple sclerosis and died September 26, 2025.

leaders.dean: Danny O. Jacobs, M.D., M.P.H., FACS
leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President, Provost and Dean of the School of Medicine
leaders.priorInstitution: University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) at Galveston
leaders.nextRole: Temporary adviser during transition, then departed
leaders.notes: OHSU's 5th president; began August 1, 2018. Announced October 24, 2024 that he was stepping down citing personal reasons after a fraught tenure (governance and workforce controversies, a stalled Legacy Health merger). His exit was effective when interim president Stadum took office November 5, 2024.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, later Special Adviser (retired Sept 2024)
leaders.notes: Interim president appointed by the OHSU board November 4, 2024, effective November 5, 2024. He had worked at OHSU earlier (left in 2016), then was EVP/COO and later special adviser at Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center until retiring in September 2024, two months before returning. His interim term ended when Elnahal began August 11, 2025.

leaders.priorTitle: Under Secretary for Health
leaders.notes: OHSU's 6th president; appointed June 27, 2025 and started August 11, 2025. Immediately prior he was the U.S. Under Secretary for Health at the VA (Senate-confirmed July 2022; resigned January 2025 at the change of administration). Harvard M.D. and M.B.A.; previously New Jersey Commissioner of Health.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice Chancellor
leaders.notes: PSU's first woman president; served 1990 to 1997 as president and professor of biology. Came from the University of Kansas (executive vice chancellor, 1987 to 1990) and left to become president of the University of Vermont (1997 to 2001).

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, School of Law
leaders.notes: PSU's first and only African-American president, serving 1997 to 2007. Previously dean of the University of Wisconsin Law School (1990 to 1997); after PSU he led the Law School Admission Council. He died September 24, 2016 (age 69).

leaders.priorTitle: Provost / Provost Emeritus
leaders.nextRole: Returned to Portland State University (Provost Emeritus / faculty)
leaders.notes: Longtime PSU insider (joined 1964 as a history professor, provost from 1992) who served as interim president 2007 to 2008 between Bernstine and Wiewel.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Served roughly nine years (2008 to 2017). Came from the University of Baltimore (provost), earlier a dean at the University of Illinois at Chicago; left PSU to become president of Lewis & Clark College effective October 1, 2017.

leaders.priorTitle: Interim President (formerly Provost)
leaders.notes: PSU's 9th president, August 2017 to May 2019. Pressured by the Board of Trustees to resign (effective May 10, 2019) amid allegations of misused funds and mistreatment of staff. Came from NYIT, where he was interim president after serving as provost.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, College of Urban and Public Affairs
leaders.notes: PSU's 10th president. First named acting/interim president in May 2019 after Shoureshi's resignation; the Board of Trustees voted unanimously in May 2020 to make him permanent. Retired July 31, 2023. Previously PSU's dean of the College of Urban and Public Affairs (since 2014).

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice Chancellor
leaders.notes: PSU's 11th president and second woman to hold the office; appointed March 10, 2023 and began August 2023. Came from the University of Pittsburgh (provost, 2018 to 2023); earlier dean at Boston University. Philosopher by training (Ph.D. Pittsburgh; B.A. Swarthmore).

leaders.priorTitle: Director of Health and Security
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Texas A&M University and Lone Star College (The Woodlands, TX)
leaders.notes: Sixth president; appointed October 1994, served until 2002 (in office in 1996, used to anchor the chain). Retired U.S. Army Major General with 38+ years of service; held the Smithsonian security-director post briefly before PVAMU. Died July 4, 2013, age 77.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Finance and Administration
leaders.notes: Interim/acting president 2002 to 2003 between Hines and Wright; had been PVAMU's VP for Finance and Administration (named 1996). Retired U.S. Army Colonel (31 years, retired 1992). Died in 2003.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs and Provost
leaders.nextRole: President Emeritus and professor of history
leaders.notes: Seventh president; took office August 15, 2003, served until June 2017. A race-relations historian, he taught history while president and returned to the faculty afterward as President Emeritus.

leaders.priorTitle: President Emerita (former university president; came out of retirement)
leaders.priorInstitution: Brown University (18th president 2001 to 2012); earlier president of Smith College
leaders.notes: Eighth president and first woman to lead PVAMU; took office July 1, 2017 on an interim basis, then appointed permanently. First African American to lead an Ivy League school (Brown). Announced early departure February 2023 and joined Rice as President's Distinguished Fellow (April 1, 2023).

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, Whitlowe R. Green College of Education
leaders.nextRole: Interim Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Acting/interim president March 1 to June 1, 2023, bridging Simmons' early departure and LeGrande's arrival. A 25-year PVAMU veteran; returned to academic-affairs leadership afterward.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Strategic Enrollment Management and Student Success
leaders.notes: Ninth president; assumed office June 1, 2023 and formally inaugurated March 2024. Second woman to lead PVAMU. Came from VCU where she led strategy, enrollment management and student success.
